summary: Fixed a floor-editor rendering bug where dragging a camera marker left its aiming furniture behind: the aim knob, the two field-of-view edge knobs, the accent lines out to them and the live heading/fov readout all read the camera's stored (pre-drag) position for the whole drag instead of the live drag preview, so the marker moved but its coverage-arc handles visibly stayed put. camHandles() in floor_editor.js is now given the previewed x/y/heading (resolved from the same drag-preview snapshot the marker and its coverage wedge already use) instead of the committed placement row while a drag is in flight. Also fixed a related, latent bug in the same code path: the coverage wedge took its position from the drag preview but its heading from the stored row, so a rotated multi-select would draw its cones still pointing the old way mid-drag; the wedge now reads heading from the preview too. Hit-testing is untouched (it correctly keeps using the committed row, since no drag is in flight when a hit test runs).
compatibility: Backward compatible - purely a rendering fix inside one frontend component, no API, schema, prop, or config changes. camHandles()'s signature is unchanged; it is only ever handed a different (position/heading-substituted) object during an active drag. No operator or migration action required.
